chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who married during her waiting period out of ignorance on her part. He said: 'I do not see any fault upon her, and they are separated from the one she married, and she does not become permissible to him forever.' The meaning in this report is that we assume he had intercourse with her; for if that is the case, she does not become permissible to him forever, whether he was ignorant or knowledgeable. And she becomes permissible with ignorance only if he had not had intercourse with her, which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who marries during her waiting period out of ignorance?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) to clarify the status of a marriage contracted during the waiting period (iddah) due to ignorance. The key scholarly distinction lies in whether consummation occurred: if intercourse took place, the marriage is considered permanently forbidden (haram) to that man, regardless of his knowledge; however, if no intercourse occurred, the marriage remains valid and she may stay with him.
